study_guide.title: The Calm in the Middle

pages.text: Last week, Cane the Weather Dog learned where hurricanes are born. This week, he wanted to know what a hurricane looks like inside. "A big hurricane has three parts," said Cane. "Let's meet them one at a time." First come the rain bands. "These are long, curving arms of rain that spiral out from the storm," said Cane. He wiggled his paw in a big curl. "They bring waves of rain — first a little, then a lot, then a little again."
pages.ask: Can you draw a big spiral in the air with your finger?

pages.text: Next, closer to the middle, is the eyewall. "This is a ring of tall, booming thunderstorms," said Cane. "And here is the important part — the eyewall has the strongest winds of the whole storm. It is the most powerful part."
pages.ask: Can you make a big wind sound — WHOOOSH — for the eyewall?

pages.text: And then… right in the very center… something surprising. "It goes calm," Cane whispered. "This is the eye. In the eye, the air sinks down, so it is quiet. The wind slows, and sometimes you can even see blue sky." "But listen closely, because this is Cane's big safety rule," said Cane, sitting up tall. "When the eye passes over, it gets calm — but the storm is NOT over. On the other side of the eye is the eyewall again, with all that strong wind, coming back."
pages.ask: Isn't that strange? A calm, quiet spot right in the middle of a giant storm!

pages.text: "So if it suddenly gets calm during a storm, we do not run outside. We stay inside and wait until a grown-up says it is really, truly safe." Cane smiled. "Now you know a hurricane inside and out — the rain bands, the eyewall, and the calm eye. And you know the smart, safe thing to do. You're a real weather watcher!"
pages.ask: What do we do if it gets suddenly calm? (Stay inside!)

study_guide.rule: The eye is calm — but the eyewall around it has the strongest winds!

cards.def: quiet and still, with little or no wind
the calm, quiet center of a hurricane
the ring around the eye — strongest winds
curving arms of rain that spiral out
heavy rain and strong wind, with thunder and lightning

questions.q: What is the calm, quiet center of a hurricane called?
Which part of a hurricane has the STRONGEST winds?
choices: the eyewall (the ring around the eye)

questions.q: What are the long, curving arms of rain that spiral out called?

choices: the air sinks there, so it is quiet

questions.q: During a storm it suddenly gets calm. What should you do?
choices: stay inside — the storm may not be over
take a nap on the porch

questions.q: When the calm eye passes over, what comes next?
choices: the eyewall again, from the other side

bonus.prompt: Name the three parts of a hurricane!
